pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to our Nursery - Cheam Common Infants' Academy
pageCache.text:
Welcome to our Nursery
Starting your child's journey with us at Cheam Common Infants’ Academy, part of the LEO Academy Trust, means they are embarking on a truly exciting adventure. Our nursery is where a love of learning begins, and we are committed to providing a safe, secure, and stimulating environment for every child.
Our Nursery Experience
We believe that learning should be fun and engaging. Our approach is centered around play-based learning, encouraging children to explore, discover, and develop new skills at their own pace. We provide a dedicated Nursery indoor and outdoor space where curiosity is sparked and friendships are made.
Our nursery features thoughtful design with 58 dedicated learning spaces across our Ducklings Room and Cygnets Room. Each room is designed to spark curiosity and learning. We also provide child-height toilets and sinks to encourage independence.
The nursery is an integral part of our school community, and our dedicated team works closely with each child to help them feel secure and happy, building the crucial foundations needed for a successful transition into Reception.
Beyond our indoor and outdoor learning areas, we have a strong focus on outdoor education. Sport Specialists within LEO ensure physical development is prioritised through a diverse range of activities designed to develop the childrens’ gross motor skills.
Our Offer
We welcome children from 3 years old to join our nursery. Our nursery operates during a variety of sessions during school term time, with session times designed to align seamlessly with the main school day, offering convenience for families. We accept all forms of government funding and childcare vouchers. For comprehensive details on sessions, fees, and available funding, please refer to our dedicated Fees, Funding, and Sessions page.
We warmly invite you to visit our nursery and meet our team. Further information on admissions and booking a visit can be found on our Admissions page.

pageCache.text:
Nursery & Reception Starters
Thank you for your interest in Cheam Common Infants' Academy. We warmly welcome In-Year applications across all of our year groups! If you are moving to the area or looking to transfer your child to our school, we would be delighted to welcome you for a visit. We are happy to offer school tours—please contact our main office directly on 020 8337 4152 to arrange your visit.
We understand that starting a new school is a significant milestone. To help ensure a smooth, happy, and confident transition for both children and parents, we have dedicated transition websites packed with essential information, helpful guides, and practical insights into daily life at Cheam Common Infants'.
Our New Starter website for the academic year 2026-2027 please click here.
We look forward to welcoming you and your family to our school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: LEO Explorers - Cheam Common Infants' Academy
pageCache.text:
LEO Explorers
LEO Academy Trust, prides itself in developing the whole child and preparing them for the next stage of their learning. We aim to develop well-rounded pupils who develop critical thinking, leadership skills, life skills and cultural capital.
This is supported through our LEO Explorer Characteristics which underpin our curriculum, empowering all pupils to embrace our LEO Pupil Outcomes.
Creating a positive and inclusive classroom environment is fundamental to the development of LEO Explorer Characteristics. We believe that by nurturing these attributes and attitudes for learning, we equip our pupils to be confident, compassionate, and capable leaders who positively impact their communities and help shape a better tomorrow.
LEO Explorer Characteristic Child Definitions
The creation of LEO explorer characteristics has been a fabulous collaboration of thoughts and ideas from a number of groups from within the LEO Team. Special thanks to everyone involved in this project with particular recognition to Niamh Wilson for bringing the LEO explorers to life with her brilliant illustrations and Evo Hannan for getting us started on this journey.

pageCache.pageTitle: PSHE & RSE - Cheam Common Infants' Academy
pageCache.text:
PSHE & RSE
Through our PSHE curriculum, at Cheam Common Infants’ Academy we aspire to instil core values such as respect, tolerance, empathy, and responsibility, promoting a sense of citizenship and community within our young learners. We want every pupil to have high aspirations, a belief in themselves and a realisation that anything is possible if they put their mind to it. When our pupils leave Cheam Common Infants’ Academy, they do so with the knowledge, understanding, skills and emotions to be able to play an active, positive and successful role in today’s society. We want to provide them with the tools to navigate challenges, express themselves, and build resilience and overall ensure they are able to develop into the most social, emotional, moral, spiritual and resilient young people they can be, allowing them to thrive in an ever changing world.
At Cheam Common Infants' we use the Jigsaw whole school approach to support teachers to champion our pupils and ensure they receive a high quality Personal, Social and Health Education which provides them with the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to lead confident, healthy, independent lives and to become informed, active and responsible citizens. Jigsaw provides a comprehensive PSHE Programme which covers all the requirements of the government guidance and outcomes, and more. It brings together Personal, Social, Health Education, emotional literacy, social skills and spiritual development in a comprehensive scheme of learning. The pupils cover six topics throughout the year;
Jigsaw is designed as a whole school approach, meaning all year groups from Nursery to Year 2 are working on the same theme (Puzzle) at the same time. This provides opportunities to embed skills and build on the pupils’s prior learning and knowledge whilst stretching and challenging them appropriately.
Relationships and Sex education (RSE) is an integral part of our PSHE curriculum. Through our Relationships unit, We teach the pupils the foundations of healthy relationships, emphasising respect, consent, communication, and empathy. As an outcome our pupils learn how to form positive connections with their peers, families, and communities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths & Financial Literacy - Cheam Common Infants' Academy
pageCache.text:
Maths & Financial Literacy
Maths
At Cheam Common Infants’ Academy, we recognise and embrace that mathematics is an important and essential part of everyday life. We provide pupils with a high-quality education through a Teaching for Mastery approach to ensure pupils have not only a deep understanding, but develop into confident mathematicians.
Using the Mastering Number scheme from Reception through to Year 2 ensures the children have a secure knowledge of additive facts which they can then apply fluently across different contexts and when problem solving.
The KS1 mathematics curriculum is based upon the NCETM CP materials which provide a deep understanding of mathematical concepts from addition, subtraction, multiplication and division to shape, space and measure. These daily lessons provide coherently planned small steps to ensure that all learners learn whilst immersing our pupils in the technical mathematical vocabulary to be able to confidently communicate their understanding of key concepts when reasoning. This is vital for developing our pupils’ metacognition.
Maths Progression Map Early Years Maths Overview
Financial Literacy
At Cheam Common, we teach the skills, knowledge, attitudes and behaviours that help people to manage money and achieve good financial wellbeing begin to develop from an early age. Research shows that financial behaviour starts to be shaped between the ages of three and seven, and long-term financial outcomes can be predicted from skills and behaviour in children as young as five.

pageCache.text:
Music
At Cheam Common Infants' Academy, we believe that music making is a powerful and personal experience that can aid children’s development in so many ways; academically, physically, socially and emotionally. Our aim is to provide every child with a high quality music education which engages, inspires and nurtures a love of music and so in turn, increases self confidence, creativity and achievement.
We are committed to providing the children with a wide variety of learning activities that include performing, composing, listening and appraising a wide variety of music from different genres, eras and cultures. Our children have the opportunity to play at least one instrument whilst they are at Cheam Common and will be able to develop an understanding and use different forms of music notation. We offer extensive range of enrichment activities which includes trips, visitors, choir, rock band, performing in high quality musical events and productions.
We deliver our Music Curriculum through the 'Sing Up' scheme of work and in collaboration with Sutton Music Service.
Music comes alive when shared with an audience, and our school takes great pride in hosting Harvest and Christmas performances in our local church. These events give our children the chance to showcase their talents, build confidence, and connect with the school community.
At Cheam Common Infants’, we believe that every child has a unique melody waiting to be heard, and we are here to help them find their voice in the world of music.
